question: A method is declared `func (c *Counter) Inc()` with a pointer receiver. Which is in the method set of the VALUE type Counter (not *Counter)?
options: Only value-receiver methods; Inc is NOT in Counter's method set
Both value- and pointer-receiver methods
Only pointer-receiver methods
Neither, because method sets apply only to interfaces
explanation: The method set of T contains only its value-receiver methods, while *T's method set contains both value- and pointer-receiver methods. So Inc belongs to *Counter's set but not Counter's, which is why only *Counter can satisfy an interface requiring Inc.

options: A map element is not addressable, so Go can't take its address for the pointer receiver
Inc must use a value receiver to work at all
Maps cannot store struct values
Inc must return a value to be called
explanation: A pointer-receiver call needs an addressable operand so Go can synthesize &operand. Map elements are not addressable, so m["a"].Inc() is a compile error. Pull the value out, mutate it, and put it back, or store *C in the map.

question: Which statement about calling a pointer-receiver method is TRUE?
options: On an addressable value, Go inserts the address-of automatically, so c.Inc() becomes (&c).Inc()
You must always write (&c).Inc() explicitly; Go never auto-addresses
Pointer-receiver methods can be called on any value, including map elements
Pointer-receiver methods copy the receiver just like value receivers
explanation: On an addressable value such as a local variable, Go automatically takes the address so c.Inc() is rewritten to (&c).Inc(). This convenience does not apply to non-addressable operands like map elements or literals, and a pointer receiver passes a pointer, not a copy.

question: You have `type Celsius float64` and want to add a ToF() method to it. Which is true?
options: It works: methods can attach to any defined type in the same package, including named types over primitives
It fails: methods can only be defined on struct types
It works only if Celsius is declared as a struct wrapping a float64
It fails: you cannot define methods on numeric types under any circumstances
explanation: You can attach methods to any defined type declared in your package, not just structs, including named types over built-ins like type Celsius float64. You just cannot add methods to types from other packages or to built-in types directly.
